messages:
Maya (sre): incident-bot paged me — Ember VPC tenants reporting elevated 5xxs on /v1/generate :rotating_light:
inc-bot: [ALERT] ember-prod-vpc: 5xx spike > 5% over 3m — routed to #incidents, oncall: @Devon (pagerid: PD123)
Devon (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing logs from the ingress layer now. Laura, are Ember users on Dedicated GPU clusters or private VPC?
Laura (acct-eng): Ember is on a private VPC connected to our dedicated pool (zone-eu-2/ember-pool). They run a pinned model policy but had a recent canary of safe-variant v2 in the pool.
Maya (sre): early signs show KV cache pressure and some OOMs on a subset of workers. Correlating with the canary rollout for safe-variant v2 — some tasks are hitting longer sequence lengths than expected.
Sam (runtime): confirmed one node is thrashing, logs show repeated kernel selection failures followed by fallback to CPU inference. I see errors like `cudaMalloc failed` and `kv_cache_miss_ratio: 0.22`.
Devon (oncall): @Sam, can we immediately route Ember's VPC traffic off problematic nodes and into spare nodes in ember-pool? If not, do we pin them back to the previously stable variant (v1)?
Sam (runtime): routing/spillover is possible but will add latency. Quickest way to restore service is to force a model pin to ember-stable:v1 for Ember tenant — that avoids the canary path.
Laura (acct-eng): Ember asked us not to change model behavior without notice, but they prefer service continuity. I've DM'd them and they approved a temporary pin for 30m with rollback later.
Devon (oncall): OK. I'll execute a tenant-level override. Command to run (platform-admin only):
```
redwoodctl tenant override set --tenant ember --model ember-stable:v1 --scope tenant --ttl 30m --reason "emergency pin to avoid OOMs during canary"
```
Devon (oncall): running now...
Devon (oncall): done. override id: ov-9c3f. routing updates propagating — consul shows epcache update, and ember-pool reports connections switching to v1.
Maya (sre): monitoring: 5xxs dropping from 6.1% -> 0.8% over 60s. Latency +60ms on average while pin is active.
inc-bot: [UPDATE] override ov-9c3f applied for tenant ember by Devon. Audit link: https://console.redwood.example/admin/overrides/ov-9c3f
Laura (acct-eng): I told Ember support team and they confirmed degraded latency is acceptable for now. They asked for a postmortem and a plan to prevent future canary cross-traffic into their VPC.
Sam (runtime): root cause hypothesis: the canary safe-variant v2 has a memory allocation pattern that isn't compatible with quantization profile used on ember-pool's GPUs. We need a safe-variant qualification checklist per pool.
Devon (oncall): action items: 1) keep override active for 30m, 2) soak monitoring and confirm no more OOMs, 3) schedule rollback canary to a staging pool, not ember-pool, 4) run post-incident config: add guardrail to prevent auto-canary into dedicated pools with tenant isolation flag.
Maya (sre): I'm creating a temporary alert rule to escalate if kv_cache_miss_ratio > 0.15 for ember pool. Also kicking off a triage runbook.
Laura (acct-eng): I'm scheduling a call with Ember SRE and product to review rollback and acceptable time windows.
OpsRun (bot): paging handoff reminder — Devon to hand off to oncall rotation (Sam) at 18:00 UTC if unresolved.
Devon (oncall): noted. If things look stable at +25m I'll close the pager and update the incident ticket.
Maya (sre): recording this thread into the incident doc: INC-2026-EMB-07. Postmortem owner: Laura. Sam, can you capture the kernel failure logs into the ticket?
Sam (runtime): will attach logs + heap dumps to INC-2026-EMB-07. Also adding reproducer script to run on staging: `tests/repro/ember-oom.sh`
Devon (oncall): ok closing loop — 5xxs at 0.4% last check, CPU fallback count down to 0. Will keep override until TTL or until we confirm safe canary in staging. Good job team. :thumbsup:
Maya (sre): leaving notes for the postmortem: consider an explicit tenant-safe-variant opt-out flag, and validate quantization profile per pool.
Laura (acct-eng): Ember replied: "thanks — prefer 2h notice before any future canary that touches our pool." Logged.
Devon (oncall): end of thread status: mitigated via tenant pin; follow-ups: postmortem, add guardrail, change canary routing.
inc-bot: [CLOSED] incident paging quieted for ember-prod-vpc — follow-ups assigned.
